AI governance

01

Under review2026 · AI for Society

Governing Frontier AI: Organizational Boundaries and the Providers of AI Governance

Sole-authored

Where does frontier-AI governance actually happen? I coded 25 documented governance-provision instances across ten developers within a twelve-developer sample, and compared them with a baseline of 51 specialist providers. The evidence shows provision across internal and external organizations, while concentrated disclosure limits what can be inferred about the wider market.

Contribution: Original disclosure coding and a comparison of developer-level governance arrangements with venture-oriented provider data.

  • Organizational economics
  • Frontier AI
  • First-party disclosures
  • Crunchbase

Labor-market institutions

02

Working paper2026 · SAIGE Incubator

Estimating Differential Routing Rates in Germany’s Federal Employment Agency

With Aileen Voit, Nafisah Animashaun and Leonard Schmidt

Using monthly administrative statistics, we document differences in occupational registration and vocational training within Germany’s unemployment-insurance regime. Flight-context jobseekers are registered for unskilled-tier occupations 1.6 times as often as the comparison group and receive substantive vocational training at half the rate. These aggregate disparities do not establish algorithmic causation.

My contribution: Designed the monitoring framework, built the bounded estimator and wrote the empirical sections.

  • Administrative statistics, 2016–2026
  • Bounded estimation
  • Labor-market policy

Methods & technical work

From questions
to evidence.

Econometric methods, machine learning, and careful measurement. Selected implementations in Python and R.

01 / CAUSAL INFERENCE

Estimating effects with DoubleML

Python · ENSAE Paris · 2025

Team project using orthogonal scores and cross-fitted nuisance models to estimate scholarship effects on dropout and graduation. Implemented preprocessing and inference.

02 / LANGUAGE MODELS

Text classification with DistilBERT

Python · University of Bonn · 2023

Fine-tuned DistilBERT for emotion classification in poetry, with text cleaning, tokenization, train-validation splitting and class-level evaluation.

03 / SIMULATION

Evaluating regression discontinuity

R · University of Bonn · 2023–24

Designed a Monte Carlo comparison of polynomial specifications, measuring finite-sample bias, variance and root mean squared error.

About me

An economist working
across boundaries.

My work connects AI governance and public finance with empirical research on firms and institutions.

I’m a doctoral researcher in macroeconomics at IWH Halle and Leipzig University, supervised by Prof. Xiang Li. Alongside my PhD, I develop AI economics research through SPAR and work on the measurement of institutional harms.
